SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence helps you remember the cardinal points in clockwise order? (1 mark)
   A. Watch Every Sunny Night
   B. Eat Slowly Now Wisely
   C. Never Eat Slimy Worms
   D. Some Old Men Walk

2. What does a compass needle point to? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. The sun
   C. The nearest town
   D. North

3. What does the size of a county mean? (1 mark)
   A. The number of roads in it
   B. The area of land it covers
   C. The number of schools in it
   D. The number of people in it

4. Where does a river usually start? (1 mark)
   A. On high land
   B. In the desert
   C. On the beach
   D. In a lake

5. Which of these is a way of caring for a river? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing rubbish into it
   B. Washing cars in it
   C. Planting trees along its banks
   D. Cutting trees at the bank

6. Who built Fort Jesus? (1 mark)
   A. The Portuguese
   B. The Kenyan government in 1990
   C. Nobody built it
   D. The British in 1950

7. Why was Fort Jesus built? (1 mark)
   A. To guard the harbour
   B. To grow food
   C. To keep cattle
   D. To make sugar

8. How do religious leaders help the community? (1 mark)
   A. They drive buses
   B. They repair roads
   C. They teach values and comfort people
   D. They sell food

9. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. All useful jobs are important
   B. Small jobs do not matter
   C. Only farming is important
   D. Only doctors are important

10. Which of these is not a reason for crowded areas? (1 mark)
   A. Very little rain and no water
   B. Fertile soil
   C. Jobs in a town
   D. Good roads

11. Why do many people live near rivers and lakes? (1 mark)
   A. Lakes have no fish
   B. Water is available for drinking and farming
   C. Rivers are dangerous
   D. Rivers are always dry

12. Which practice do Kenyan laws forbid because it harms girls? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking ugali
   B. Female genital mutilation
   C. Playing bao
   D. Wearing beads

13. Why is traditional culture important? (1 mark)
   A. It has no use
   B. It gives identity and teaches values
   C. It makes people fight
   D. It stops all change

14. Which resource gives electric power from underground steam at Olkaria? (1 mark)
   A. Coal
   B. Geothermal heat
   C. Wind
   D. Oil

15. Which crop is grown mainly in sugarcane growing areas of Western Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Coffee
   B. Tea
   C. Sugarcane
   D. Wheat

16. What is the raw material for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Sugarcane
   B. Milk
   C. Tea leaves
   D. Wheat

17. What is a project? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of fruit
   B. A plan of work with a start, a finish and a goal
   C. A holiday
   D. A type of shoe

18. Which action shows respect? (1 mark)
   A. Ignoring teachers
   B. Greeting teachers politely
   C. Breaking desks
   D. Insulting classmates

19. Which school transport is safe? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger's car
   B. A vehicle approved by school and parents
   C. A vehicle with no seats
   D. An overloaded vehicle

20. Which of these can you call for help in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A shop
   B. A cinema
   C. The child helpline 116
   D. A bakery

21. Which action helps a child with special needs? (1 mark)
   A. Including them in games
   B. Neglecting them
   C. Laughing at them
   D. Hiding them

22. Which of these can cause child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Enough food
   B. Good schools
   C. Poverty and harmful beliefs
   D. Kind neighbours

23. What is a candidate? (1 mark)
   A. A cleaner
   B. A voter
   C. A teacher
   D. A person who stands to be elected

24. Who leads a clan? (1 mark)
   A. Clan elders
   B. A cook
   C. A bus driver
   D. A footballer

25. Which activity can show leadership qualities in class? (1 mark)
   A. Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   B. Sleeping
   C. Fighting
   D. Copying

26. Which quality means not boasting or looking down on others? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Humility
   C. Greed
   D. Pride

27. Which of these tasks belongs to the county government? (1 mark)
   A. Foreign affairs
   B. County roads
   C. National defence
   D. Immigration

28. Who is closest to the people among county administrators? (1 mark)
   A. The governor
   B. The president
   C. The village administrator
   D. The speaker

29. What does the county assembly do? (1 mark)
   A. Drives buses
   B. Trains footballers
   C. Makes county laws and approves the budget
   D. Cooks meals

30. Who is the head of the national government? (1 mark)
   A. The Speaker
   B. The MCA
   C. The President
   D. The Governor

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List four questions you could ask to find out the history of your school. (4 marks)

32. Explain four ways in which rainy weather makes roads dangerous. (4 marks)

33. A group spent Ksh 350 on seeds and Ksh 150 on tools. They sold vegetables for Ksh 800. Find the profit. Show working. (3 marks)

34. Give three things that should be on a sketch map of your county. (3 marks)

35. Draw a weather chart for three days: sunny, rainy, cloudy. Add a key. (3 marks)

36. Give three reasons why people need directions in everyday life. (3 marks)

37. Give four duties of a religious leader. (4 marks)

38. A weather chart for a week shows: Mon sunny, Tue sunny, Wed rainy, Thu cloudy, Fri rainy, Sat sunny, Sun cloudy. How many days were sunny, rainy and cloudy? (3 marks)

39. Explain how good citizenship in school prepares pupils to be good citizens of Kenya. (4 marks)

40. Give three questions to ask when choosing a school enterprise project. (3 marks)

41. State three qualities of a good citizen in school and give an example for each. (3 marks)

42. Give three qualities of a good leader and explain why each matters. (3 marks)

43. Explain what would happen in a community if farmers stopped growing food. (4 marks)

44. Describe two peace-building activities that a school can carry out. (4 marks)

45. What is a majority? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Never Eat Slimy Worms
   The first letters N, E, S, W give north, east, south, west in clockwise order.

2. D — North
   A magnetic compass needle always turns to point north.

3. B — The area of land it covers
   Size means the area of land, not the population.

4. A — On high land
   Rivers start on high land and flow to lower land.

5. C — Planting trees along its banks
   Trees hold the soil and keep the water clean.

6. A — The Portuguese
   The Portuguese built the fort more than 400 years ago.

7. A — To guard the harbour
   It was built as a stone fort to guard the harbour.

8. C — They teach values and comfort people
   Religious leaders teach good values and care for people.

9. A — All useful jobs are important
   Every worker contributes to the community.

10. A — Very little rain and no water
   Dryness with no water makes areas sparse.

11. B — Water is available for drinking and farming
   Water is a basic need.

12. B — Female genital mutilation
   FGM is against the law.

13. B — It gives identity and teaches values
   Culture helps us to know who we are.

14. B — Geothermal heat
   Olkaria makes electricity from geothermal steam.

15. C — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane is grown in parts of Western Kenya.

16. A — Sugarcane
   Sugar is made from sugarcane.

17. B — A plan of work with a start, a finish and a goal
   A project is planned work for a goal.

18. B — Greeting teachers politely
   Polite greetings show respect.

19. B — A vehicle approved by school and parents
   Approved vehicles are safer.

20. C — The child helpline 116
   Childline Kenya can be reached on 116.

21. A — Including them in games
   Children with special needs have equal rights.

22. C — Poverty and harmful beliefs
   Poverty and harmful beliefs are causes.

23. D — A person who stands to be elected
   Candidates ask for votes.

24. A — Clan elders
   Clan elders lead the clan.

25. A — Role-playing an elder settling a quarrel
   Role play shows how leaders act.

26. B — Humility
   Humble leaders are modest.

27. B — County roads
   County roads belong to the county.

28. C — The village administrator
   Village administrators work closest to families.

29. C — Makes county laws and approves the budget
   The assembly makes laws and approves the budget.

30. C — The President
   The President leads the national government.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: When was the school started? Who started it? Who was the first headteacher? How has the school changed?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each relevant question.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roads become slippery, it is harder to see, floods can sweep away people and vehicles, and water can hide holes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 300.
   Working / marking points: Cost = 350 + 150 = 500. Profit = 800 - 500 = 300. 1 mark for cost, 1 mark for subtraction, 1 mark for answer.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: A title, a north arrow and a key. Accept sub-county names and boundaries.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Three boxes with a sun, a cloud with rain lines and a plain cloud, and a key that names each symbol.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct symbols, 1 mark for the days, 1 mark for the key.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: To find places, to travel safely, and to explain to others where something is. Accept sailors, pilots and farmers using direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Lead prayers, teach values, counsel people and visit the sick. Accept conducting weddings or funerals.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 sunny days, 2 rainy days and 2 cloudy days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct count. Check: 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 days.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Pupils learn to follow rules, respect others, take care of public property and take responsibility. These habits continue when they are adults.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do people want it? Do we have the materials and skills? Is it safe? Can we earn more than we spend?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty: returning lost items. Respect: greeting teachers. Responsibility: doing class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with example.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty so people trust the leader, fairness so all are treated equally, and listening so decisions are wise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality with reason.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: There would be a shortage of food. Traders would have nothing to sell. Prices would go up. People could become hungry and ill.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each consequence.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: A peace garden where pupils can sit calmly and a peace poster competition to teach about peace. Explain how each helps.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity and 1 mark for each explanation.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The larger number of votes, more than any other choice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for larger number, 1 mark for votes.
